text:
Philadelphia arrives with a 3-2 win over Colorado two days ago, but the Flyers are thin up front. Owen Tippett and Travis Konecny are both on injured reserve, with Cam York and Rasmus Ristolainen also out. Buffalo comes in off a 4-3 overtime loss at Montreal, where Cole Caufield won it, and is missing Matt Grzelcyk, though Rasmus Dahlin is now day-to-day and could return. The Sabres are better than their record: they've had 51% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) this season, but finishing and goaltending have cost them.

The gap shows at five on five, where Buffalo has taken 53% of the expected goals to Philadelphia's 35%. The Flyers also take 4.2 penalties a game, which keeps handing out power plays. In net, projected starters Dan Vladar and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen are both below expected this season, but each was well above it last year. With Konecny out, Tyson Foerster has moved beside Christian Dvorak and Matvei Michkov, and Denver Barkey has taken a first power-play spot. Our model has Buffalo at 3.0 expected goals tonight and Philadelphia at 2.65.

Watch Tage Thompson, who has a 41% chance to score and 70% to get a point. Trevor Zegras, on the top power play, is at 26% to score. Zach Benson is Ice Sheet's under-the-radar pick: he's at 57% for a point, above his season pace, because his line creates chances.
